actual: Auto-filed issues such as GitHub Issue #197 contain only generic CI failure metadata and no failed test or error details; the current workflow uses run-id markers and does not bridge GitHub CI issues into BUG JSON workflow commands.
closure_requirements: Auto-filed CI/Nightly issues include failed job, nox session or failed step, failed test or error signature, key log excerpt, reproduce command, diagnostic status, production gates, and fingerprint marker.
Repeated failures with the same fingerprint update the existing GitHub Issue instead of creating duplicate run-id-only issues.
If log extraction is partial or unavailable, the issue explicitly records diagnostic_status=partial plus extraction errors and uses needs-log-triage semantics rather than creating an empty issue.
Repo workflow CLI supports triage-ci-issue and promote-ci-issue so Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or humans can move from GitHub Issue to BUG JSON and then standard run --bug-id workflow.
BUG-119 JSON and GitHub Issue #202 stay synchronized, and validation evidence covers parser, workflow CLI, ownership, and catalog gates.

events.note: Expanded BUG-119 scope and closure requirements after implementing CI failure summary extraction, fingerprint dedupe, and triage/promote CLI bridge.

expected: CI/Nightly failure intake creates or updates a diagnostic-rich GitHub Issue with failed job/session/test/error details, fingerprint-based dedupe, partial extraction status when needed, and a repo CLI path to triage/promote the issue into BUG JSON before standard worktree-based repair.
non_goals: Do not restart production runtime services without explicit approval.
